sections.heading: C - You the Driver
sections.markdown:
## C - You the Driver

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Safe driving needs hands, eyes, and mind fully engaged, regular vision, hearing, and body checkups, and a medication consult on driving effects [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Older drivers should schedule regular medical and eye exams, ask how medications—especially in combination—affect driving, stay flexible and strong through exercise, make needed vehicle adjustments, avoid sunglasses in dim or dark conditions, and avoid dusk, dawn, nighttime, bad weather, rush-hour traffic, and fast-paced highways [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
The state mobility-for-life program schools older adults, families, caregivers, and partners on lasting safe travel [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A02
Distraction splits into visual, manual, and cognitive kinds, texting spans all three and is illegal, and handheld use is barred in school crossings, school zones, and work zones [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A02
Further distractions run from phones, gawking, reaching, passengers, food, pets, and grooming to dials, cigarettes, and daydreams [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A03
Alcohol strikes judgment first, then reflexes, sight, and distance sense, and even a single drink bars safe driving [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A03
Drunk driving risks fines, insurance pain, license loss, jail, and a 75-year record stain, so riders name a sober driver or call for a ride [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A03
Drowsy driving rivals drunk driving through dulled thought and senses plus microsleep, and yields to real sleep, breaks every 100 miles or 2 hours, naps, and buddy drivers [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A04
Drug impairment matches alcohol penalties, prescription and store-bought remedies need label and doctor checks, mixing multiplies harm, and illegal drugs warp reflexes and confidence [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A04
Worry, excitement, tears, anger, and gloom all steal focus, so drivers calm down before starting [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A04
Road rage shows in tailgating, blocking, horn and light abuse, threats, gestures, ramming, confrontations, weapons, and thrown objects, and victims add distance, yield, avoid eyes and gestures, and call for help [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0044]

items.why: Section four is condition and behavior recall served by standard flashcards and quizzes; no separate practice mode is needed.

corpus_stability.reason: The Official Florida Driver License Handbook is a dated revision (rev. 08/2023) reissued at most annually, so driver-condition rules change at most once per year.
